The opening continues a preceding sentence and writes an Aut comparison followed by a small inserted definition. The first paragraph describes a cellular decomposition with the written vertex, edge and face counts, followed by an inserted qualifier and ces arêtes. The middle paragraph describes another decomposition using the written 2 id expression and retains the replacement of the crossed number word by huit and the raised 4 before faces. The lower paragraph introduces the written quotient, calls it a sphere, retains faces above crossed deux and the subsequent equator description, and gives the four point labels and two sphere sketches. These are source statements only. This reader performed no independent proof, re-proof, mathematical computation or formal certificate; check_events is empty. The full scan and both supplied halves were each read once, followed by all eighteen planned crops and one expressly requested completion crop for the previously clipped raised part of the inserted formula. Every body baseline, formula, numeral, insertion, cancellation and drawing was inspected. The original images were read visually; no OCR, external research or TeX compilation was used. H's drawing descriptions are represented by source-based TikZ reconstructions. These decisions preserve the visible ink without mathematical repair.

Root check 148_scan007-CHECK-i-on-2torsion (base lattice explicitly written on 148_scan005). The classes killed by 2 in C/Z[i] have representatives (a+bi)/2 with a,b in {0,1}: reducing the integer real and imaginary numerators modulo 2 gives exactly those four classes. Multiplication by i sends the numerator pair (a,b) to (-b,a) modulo 2. The exact enumeration in scripts/check_square_two_torsion.py and work/square_two_torsion_check.json gives 0 -> 0, 1/2 -> i/2, i/2 -> 1/2, and (1+i)/2 -> (1+i)/2. This verifies the two-element fixed set for that displayed base lattice and the exchange of the two other nonzero 2-torsion classes described at the end of 148_scan005. The opening of 148_scan007 literally says « l'unique élément » and its inserted formula lists {e, eta_S}; the preceding page has already specified an element of order 2. No « non nul » or other clarifying words are supplied to the transcription. This finite calculation does not settle the shape of the disputed superscript or the crowded stroke beside i. Blind audit: a small raised arc beside the inserted 4 is retained; its identity is unresolved. Angular grid projections and uneven detached rear-sphere segments are reproduced. The canceled argument retains S/2 and the crowded adjective and connective endings retain alternatives. None of these decisions was supplied by an expected formula.
